Number one fit's profiles like another's

Source: R/align-labels.R
align_labels.Rd

Profiles and latent classes have no natural order, so two fits of the same model to different samples, waves or subgroups usually number them differently. align_labels() renumbers the profiles of fit, and its group classes in a two-level model, so that each takes the label of the most similar profile (group class) of reference. Nothing is re-estimated: the log likelihood, the estimates and every assignment are the same, under new labels.

Usage

align_labels(fit, reference)

Arguments

fit

A fit from lpa(), lca(), multilpa() or multilca(), with or without membership covariates.

reference

A fit of the same kind whose labels fit takes: the same indicators, coded the same way, and the same numbers of profiles and group classes.

Value

fit, of the same class, with its profiles (and group classes) renumbered: every table of get_results(), the assignments and the posterior probabilities follow the new labels. Raises latents_bad_argument when either object is not a profile or class model, or when the two fits differ in their indicators, how they are coded (the message names each categorical or ordinal indicator whose categories or their order differ), or their numbers of profiles or group classes.

Details

Profiles are matched on their measurement parameters (means, variances and, when both fits estimate them, correlations; response probabilities; ordinal and count parameters), measured in the reference's units, with each profile's share as a tie-breaker. Every permutation is tried for up to seven profiles, and each reference profile takes its nearest unclaimed match above that. Group classes are then matched on the profile mixture each carries. A membership-covariate fit may be aligned to the same model without covariates: its share is the mean posterior probability, and its membership logits are re-expressed against the new last profile. This is the alignment the cluster bootstrap, sensitivity() and pool_imputations() use.

See also

compare_models() to compare fits on their criteria.

Examples

first_days <- subset(student_esm, day <= 3)
last_days <- subset(student_esm, day > 3)
feelings <- c("happy", "exhausted")
early <- lpa(first_days, feelings, n_profiles = 2, n_starts = 2, seed = 1)
late <- lpa(last_days, feelings, n_profiles = 2, n_starts = 2, seed = 1)
# The later days' fit numbers the same two profiles the other way round.
get_results(early, "profiles")
#>   profile indicator     mean  variance standard_deviation mean_standard_error
#> 1       1     happy 5.565861 0.9550211          0.9772518          0.07763166
#> 2       1 exhausted 1.933072 0.6632697          0.8144137          0.06909314
#> 3       2     happy 4.077278 2.4600442          1.5684528          0.09053118
#> 4       2 exhausted 4.587211 2.0688916          1.4383642          0.11336925
#>   variance_standard_error
#> 1              0.10918578
#> 2              0.07583124
#> 3              0.18442118
#> 4              0.20080060
get_results(late, "profiles")
#>   profile indicator     mean  variance standard_deviation mean_standard_error
#> 1       1     happy 4.474893 2.5181753          1.5868760          0.04508037
#> 2       1 exhausted 4.022386 2.4217003          1.5561813          0.05167207
#> 3       2     happy 6.143550 0.6715874          0.8195043          0.04742078
#> 4       2 exhausted 1.322795 0.2250344          0.4743780          0.02741166
#>   variance_standard_error
#> 1              0.09858709
#> 2              0.10232709
#> 3              0.05341941
#> 4              0.01776771
get_results(align_labels(late, early), "profiles")
#>   profile indicator     mean  variance standard_deviation mean_standard_error
#> 1       1     happy 6.143550 0.6715874          0.8195043          0.04742078
#> 2       1 exhausted 1.322795 0.2250344          0.4743780          0.02741166
#> 3       2     happy 4.474893 2.5181753          1.5868760          0.04508037
#> 4       2 exhausted 4.022386 2.4217003          1.5561813          0.05167207
#>   variance_standard_error
#> 1              0.05341941
#> 2              0.01776771
#> 3              0.09858709
#> 4              0.10232709
